narr: Widespread amounts of three to five inches of rainfall were observed across the mountains and foothills during the 24-hour period ending with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta across the lower mid-Atlantic region. Despite its rapid speed across the region, the storm brought two to three inches of rain across portions of Wilkes and Surry Counties during a single hour, resulting in widespread flooding of many creeks and streams. The flooding was severe enough in some cases to wash out the bridges passing over these creeks. Lesser flooding was observed elsewhere across the Highlands of North Carolina where the rainfall rates were not as intense.
ev: Heavy rain from Tropical Storm Zeta caused Whittier Creek to overflow its banks and completely wash out Nurse Road, making the road impassible. Water was estimated to be flowing about two feet over the bridge before it was destroyed.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations indicate that more than half of the rain fell within a 2-hour period as the center of the storm passed. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Ararat community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded. A few bridges were damaged or destroyed.

Two swift-water rescues were performed for the occupants of vehicles that became stranded where Hiatt Road passes across Stoney Creek. The road was flooded and impassible for several hours. This flooding was the result of heavy rain which occurred during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta.

Between two and four inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Dobson community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded. A few bridges were damaged or destroyed. Highway 601 was impassible due to flooding of Bear Creek, where one swift water rescue was performed for an automobile that became stranded in the flood waters. Fisher River Park was also closed due to flooding.

Several roads were observed flooded and closed in and around the community of Jonesville. Among them, over six inches of water from the nearby Yadkin River was observed flowing rapidly over Fabric Lane.

Multiple privately-owned weather stations indicate that between 2 and 2.5 inches of rain fell during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Soils were already very moist due to rounds of rain that passed across the region earlier in the night. Runoff from the rain caused Cranberry Creek to overflow its banks across a bridge on Double Springs Church Road, making the bridge impassible for several hours.

Privately-owned weather stations across northern Ashe County indicate that 1.5 to slightly over 2 inches of rain fell across soils already very moist from rainfall earlier in the past 24 hours. This caused flooding of Helton Creek, overflowing across a bridge along Jim Duvall Road.

Extensive flooding took place along Cub Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as two to three inches of rain fell across the basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a one hour period, on top of an additional one to two inches that fell during the previous evening for a total of nearly five inches in 24 hours. Virtually all of Cub Creek Park was flooded, and the bridge on South Bridge Street that crosses the creek was completely over-topped by the flooded creek. Elsewhere, the dam of a 3.5 acre pond collapsed at around 1:40 pm EST, sending flood water that washed out at 20 foot section of Woodfield Way just downstream. Concern for the bridge on Industrial Park Road that crosses the creek about one mile downstream prompted evacuations of multiple businesses and apartments that would be cut off if the that bridge too was washed out, though it did not. Country Club Extension Road along Little Cub Creek was flooded and closed, as was Westover Road, where storage buildings and nearby residences were also flooded.

Extensive flooding took place along Moravian Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period. This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours. Newspaper reports indicate that nearly all of Moravian Creek was out of its banks, causing flooding Wilkes Community College's lower campus. School Street further downstream was also closed by the flood waters.

Numerous businesses along Wilkesboro Boulevard from the Yadkin River bridge to Memorial Park were flooded when the Yadkin River swiftly rose out of its banks, the result of 4 to 5 inches or rain within a 24-hour period both preceding and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations observed 2-3 inches of rain within a 1-hour period just before the onset of flooding. Flash flooding ended as the river crested during mid-afternoon, and roads were reopened during the evening once the river receded. Among the businesses flooded were Extreme Collision Auto Body, which had to move several vehicles to prevent them from being damaged by flood waters. Flood waters completely inundated Memorial Park as well as the Yadkin River Greenway.

The Reddies River at Wilkesboro (REDN7) crested at 11.79 feet (6760 cfs), which was between a 5- and 10-year Annual Return Interval per USGS StreamStats. These rises were the result of 3-5 inches of rainfall within a 24-hour period, much of which fell within a 2-hour period during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. The rapid rises resulted in the precautionary evacuation of residents from the Rose Glen Manor assisted living facility, though flooding did not enter the buildings. Employees of other nearby businesses were evacuated as well out of precaution.

Widespread flooding took place along Fishing Creek during the late morning and afternoon hours as 2 to 3 inches of rain fell across this basin with the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, most of it within a 1-hour period. This rain was in addition to another 1 to 2 inches that fell during the previous evening, for a total of nearly 5 inches in 24 hours. Newspaper reports indicate that Fishing Creek Arbor Road at Fishing Creek was washed out when the culvert running beneath the road failed. Further downstream, flood waters from the creek carried away several dozen propane gas storage tanks. It is unclear how many tanks were recovered and still functioning. In addition, high water rescues were conducted for cars that became stranded in the flood waters. One rescue was conducted on Highway 115 near the intersection with Speedway Road, and the other was on Speedway Road near the Fishing Creek Road intersection.

Moravian Creek quickly rose out of its banks during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta, the result of three to five inches of rain within a 24-hour period. This caused several roads intersecting the creek to be flooded and closed until the flood water receded, including Germantown Road and Falls Road near the Moravian Falls waterfall.

Reports of 2 to 2.5 inches of rain caused rapid river rises along the South Fork of the New River. At least one low bridge was flooded along Boggs Road, making the bridge impassible for several hours.
Flooding due to heavy rain caused by Tropical Storm Zeta resulted in flooding along the Middle Fork of the Reddies River. Colvard Road was flooded and closed for several hours as a result.

Heavy rain across central and western Wilkes County due to the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta caused rapid river rises along the Yadkin River. The Yadkin River quickly rose out of its banks, flooding multiple roads in the Roaring River and Ronda communities, including Red, White and Blue Road, Roaring River Road and Clingman Road.

Between 2 and 4 inches of rainfall occurred in the hours before and during the passage of Tropical Storm Zeta. Multiple personal weather stations indicate that more than half of the rain fell within a 2-hour period as the center of the storm passed. The heavy rain caused widespread flooding of small creeks and streams, pushing many out of their banks. Several roads, both within the Elkin community and the surrounding area, were flooded and impassible until flooding receded, including Commerce Street, Pleasant Hill Road, and Memorial Park Drive. A debris flow was reported on Johnson Ridge Road.
